key_insight: Optimize the marginal output distribution P(y) by applying reinforcement learning in the pre-train space, so reasoning ability becomes encoded as a prior rather than being limited by the base model's conditional outputs P(y|x). This unlocks broader exploration and higher ceiling for downstream RL fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Reinforcement learning that optimizes P(y|x) (RLVR) is constrained by the base model's output distribution, preventing discovery of richer reasoning behaviors and limiting improvement.
method: Reframe the training objective from conditional P(y|x) optimization to marginal P(y) optimization in the pre-train space.
Apply reinforcement learning signals (verifiable rewards) during pre-training/representation shaping to encode reasoning priors into the model's marginal distribution.
Preserve exploration by augmenting pre-train signals or dynamics so the model can generate diverse candidate outputs rather than remain bounded by static corpora.
impact: Encodes reasoning ability as a model-level prior, raising the attainable performance when later fine-tuning with RLVR and improving generalization to novel tasks. Practitioners can overcome base-model distributional ceilings and get more robust downstream reasoning with the same RL toolkit.
visual_elements: Comparison diagram: narrow P(y|x)-centered distribution (pre-RLVR) vs. broadened/more capable P(y) after pre-train-space RL
Pipeline flowchart: pre-training -> RL in pre-train (representation) space -> downstream RLVR fine-tuning
Before/after density plots or histograms showing output distribution coverage and diversity
Icon set: brain (reasoning prior), compass (exploration), and reward badge (verifiable rewards)
paper_title: From $P(y|x)$ to $P(y)$: Investigating Reinforcement Learning in Pre-train Space
paper_authors: Yuqiao Tan, Minzheng Wang, Bo Liu, Zichen Liu, Tian Liang
